prompt_payload.task: Design a diverse library of executable semantic optimization skills for finite-pool scientific search. Each skill defines interpretable rule features plus a conservative Bayesian linear surrogate blended with strong target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI anchors.

target.title: MoleculeNet Lipophilicity replay
target.boundary: Field values and counts are public; target outcomes are not included.

source_transfer_evidence.boundary: Only source identity, objective, and public source-target field alignment are provided. Source outcomes, effects, support counts, and value priors are withheld.

executor.semantic_model: Rules become binary features. Revealed target outcomes fit a ridge Bayesian linear surrogate whose coefficient prior follows rule weights.
executor.anchor: A rank blend of target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI.
executor.fusion: semantic_mass_start/end controls the rank mass assigned to the semantic surrogate; the remaining mass stays on the target-only anchor.
executor.selection: Independent calibration seeds select one frozen skill. Independent held-out seeds are evaluated only after selection.

design_requirements: Use only exact field/value pairs in public_semantic_fields.

Each conditions object must map a real catalog field name directly to one exact catalog value, for example {"dominant_family": "oxide"}. Never use literal placeholder keys such as exact_field, field_name, field, or value.
Give every skill a distinct, descriptive scientific skill_id. Never copy schema placeholders such as short_unique_name or add numeric suffixes to a placeholder.
Give every skill 3-10 rules; use two-condition interactions only when scientifically meaningful.
Include at least one conservative low-semantic-mass skill.
Include at least one skill grounded only in the supplied source-target field alignment; do not imply that source outcome effects were observed.
Include at least one domain-knowledge skill.
Include a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses or downweights an uncertain source relation.
Prefer mechanistic, chemically or physically interpretable rules over arbitrary coverage rules.
Use positive weights for conditions expected to improve the target objective and negative weights for risks.
Do not claim access to target outcomes and do not output candidate identifiers.

rules.rationale: short scientific rationale

skills.hypothesis: what this skill transfers and when it may fail

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: real_suzuki_miyaura to real_buchwald_hartwig
cards.summary: All evidence modes failed calibration and fell back to the target acquisition portfolio.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.summary: The router selected GP-UCB; the descriptive held-out strongest target portfolio remained higher on the 20-seed development range.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: counter_hypothesis_low_hbond_donors
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_esol, use the LLM to define the counter_hypothesis_low_hbond_donors feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Execution: target_calibrated. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

care_knowledge_context.instruction: Use these public, previously archived cards only as reusable design lessons. Do not copy reported target values into a rule and do not imply that the current target outcomes were observed. Prefer lessons that survived held-out calibration.

rules.rationale: High aromatic content increases hydrophobicity via pi-stacking and reduced polarity.
Fewer heteroatoms reduce hydrogen bonding capacity, favoring lipid solubility.
Moderate halogenation increases lipophilicity through hydrophobic surface area without excessive molecular weight.
High branching can disrupt crystal packing, enhancing solubility in lipids.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the principle that aromaticity and low polarity enhance lipophilicity; may fail for molecules where halogenation or branching leads to unfavorable steric effects.

rules.rationale: Source schema maps heteroatoms to solubility; high heteroatoms may reduce lipophilicity as a counter-hypothesis.
Source schema maps ring complexity; high rings may increase rigidity and lipophilicity.
Source schema maps rotatable bonds to flexibility; moderate branching may balance flexibility and lipophilicity.
Source schema maps SMILES length; moderate length may indicate optimal molecular size for lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Grounds rules only in source-target field alignment without observed effects; may fail if source solubility relationships inversely correlate with target lipophilicity.

rules.rationale: Combination of moderate halogenation and high aromaticity synergistically enhances lipophilicity through hydrophobic and electron-withdrawing effects.
Few double bonds reduce polarity, favoring lipid environments.
High ring count increases molecular rigidity and hydrophobic surface area.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the mechanistic synergy between halogenation and aromaticity for lipophilicity; may fail for molecules with steric clashes or excessive halogenation.

rules.rationale: Complete absence of heteroatoms maximizes hydrophobicity by eliminating polar interactions.
No halogens maintains a pure hydrocarbon character, enhancing lipid solubility.
Low aromaticity allows flexible aliphatic chains that favor lipid integration.
Moderate branching prevents crystallization, maintaining fluidity in lipid phases.

skills.hypothesis: Domain knowledge emphasizes pure hydrocarbons for lipophilicity; may fail for molecules requiring some polarity for membrane penetration or specific interactions.

rules.rationale: Counter-hypothesis: low ring complexity may increase flexibility but reduce hydrophobic surface, potentially lowering lipophilicity.
Source alignment uncertain; high heteroatoms may not consistently reduce lipophilicity, treated as a risk.
Moderate SMILES length suggests stable molecular size without excessive polarity.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses or downweights uncertain source relations, particularly ring complexity; may fail if source correlations hold positively for lipophilicity.

rules.rationale: High branching creates steric hindrance that disrupts aqueous solvation, favoring lipids.
High ring count adds steric bulk, increasing hydrophobic volume.
Few double bonds reduce planar rigidity, allowing conformational flexibility that enhances lipid mixing.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers steric hindrance as a driver of lipophilicity; may fail for overly bulky molecules that cannot integrate into lipid bilayers.

rules.rationale: Very long SMILES may indicate high molecular weight or complexity, potentially reducing lipophilicity due to size limitations.
No aromaticity allows fully aliphatic structures that can be highly hydrophobic.

skills.hypothesis: Conservative skill with minimal semantic influence, relying heavily on target-only anchors; may fail if simple rules miss complex lipophilicity interactions.

rules.rationale: High halogen content provides strong electron-withdrawing effects, increasing hydrophobicity and membrane permeability.
Moderate aromaticity offers pi-systems for electron delocalization, synergizing with halogens.
Low heteroatom count minimizes electron-donating groups, preserving hydrophobic character.
High double bond count enables conjugation, enhancing electron withdrawal and rigidity for lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers electron-withdrawing effects as key to lipophilicity; may fail for molecules where excessive halogenation leads to toxicity or poor bioavailability.
